per_question.question: How does NC Medicaid define 'terminally ill' for purposes of hospice eligibility, and what certification is required?

I have enough to answer the core question from the federal certification text plus NC Medicaid’s hospice policy, but I want the NC eligibility section too in case it expressly ties eligibility to being terminally ill.**NC Medicaid hospice uses the standard hospice definition of “terminally ill”:** the person’s **prognosis is a life expectancy of 6 months or less if the illness runs its normal course**. That appears in the certification requirements for hospice and is the operative standard for eligibility. See **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, Section 5.4.1 — "Timing of certification"** [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment) and **42 CFR Part 418, Section 418.22 — "Certification of terminal illness"** [42 CFR Part 418](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-418).

## Required certification

### 1) A written certification of terminal illness is required
NC Medicaid’s hospice policy says:

- the hospice provider must obtain **written certification of terminal illness for each benefit period**; and
- the written certification must be obtained **before the hospice submits a claim for payment**.

If the written certification cannot be obtained within **2 calendar days after a period begins**, an **oral certification** must be obtained within those 2 days, and the written certification must still be obtained before billing. See **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, Section 5.4.1 — "Timing of certification"** [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment).

### 2) What the certification must say
Federal hospice regulations require that the certification:

- be based on the physician’s or medical director’s **clinical judgment**; and
- **specify that the individual’s prognosis is for a life expectancy of 6 months or less if the terminal illness runs its normal course**.

The regulation also requires supporting clinical documentation and a physician narrative explaining the clinical findings supporting the prognosis. See **42 CFR Part 418, Section 418.22 — "Certification of terminal illness"** [42 CFR Part 418](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-418).

## Who must certify

### Initial 90-day benefit period
For the **initial 90-day period**, NC Medicaid requires written certification from:

- **the hospice medical director or the physician member of the hospice interdisciplinary group (IDG)**; and
- **the individual’s attending physician, if the individual has an attending physician**.

See **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, Section 5.4.3 — "Sources of certification"** [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment).

### Subsequent benefit periods
For **subsequent periods**, NC Medicaid requires certification only by:

- **the hospice medical director**, or
- **the physician member of the hospice interdisciplinary group**.

See **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, Section 5.4.3 — "Sources of certification"** [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment).

## Initial vs. later recertifications
NC Medicaid follows the standard hospice benefit periods:

- **initial 90-day period**
- **second 90-day period**
- **unlimited subsequent 60-day periods**

See **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, Section 5.7 — "Duration of Hospice Care Coverage Benefit Periods"** [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment) and **42 CFR Part 418, Section 418.21 — "Duration of hospice care coverage—Election periods"** [42 CFR Part 418](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-418).

## Face-to-face requirement for later recertifications
For the **3rd benefit period recertification and every recertification after that**, NC Medicaid requires a **face-to-face encounter** with the beneficiary by:

- a **hospice physician**, or
- a **hospice nurse practitioner**,

and it must occur **before, but no more than 30 calendar days before**, the recertification for that period. See **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, Section 5.4.1 — "Timing of certification"** [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment).

## Short answer
For NC Medicaid hospice, **“terminally ill” means the patient is certified as having a prognosis of 6 months or less if the illness runs its normal course**. The hospice must obtain **written certification for each benefit period**. For the **initial 90-day period**, the certification must come from the **hospice medical director or hospice IDG physician, plus the attending physician if there is one**. For **later periods**, only the **hospice medical director or hospice IDG physician** must certify. For the **3rd and later benefit periods**, a **face-to-face encounter** is also required before recertification.
